name: Databricks theme palette
note: Single source of truth for every colour used by the two theme files. Only the values under `brand` are official Databricks brand colours; everything under `ramps`, `supporting` and `terminalBright` is extrapolated from them so the theme has enough steps to work with. Swap values here (and regenerate/adjust the theme JSON) to re-tune the whole theme in one place.

lava.note: Accent ramp. `lava600` is the brand colour; the other steps are derived. Numbering skips 500 so `lava600` keeps the official 'Lava 600' name.

navy.note: Neutral spine. `navy800` and `navy900` are brand colours; the lighter steps and `navy850` (the dark-variant surface, sitting between the two brand navies) are derived.

oat.note: Light neutrals. `oatWhite`, `oatLight` and `oatMedium` are brand colours; `oatDark` and `oatDeep` are derived.

supporting.note: Syntax and status hues, harmonised with the brand and kept desaturated so Lava stays the loudest colour on screen. The same role keeps the same hue family in both variants; only lightness shifts.

terminalBright.note: Derived one step per supporting hue so all 16 ANSI slots can be filled with readable colours. Light-mode brights go deeper (a lighter 'bright' is unreadable on an Oat background); dark-mode brights go lighter.

roles.note: How the ramps map onto each variant. The theme JSON files are the authority; this block documents the intent.

alpha.note: Alpha suffixes used for translucent layers, so selection, find match and word highlight stack legibly.
